Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Friday. Attached are Stratos' redlines to the MSA and a short note from our legal team (Anil is cc'd). Our primary open item is the carve-out/exclusion bucket for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages. Procurement is pushing for a one-way exclusion (customer-facing) with very limited carve-outs.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirmation you can accept a one-way exclusion (i.e., Redwood remains liable for a broader set of damages) or, alternatively, provide sample mutual language.
- If mutual is required, we need clear definitions of "consequential", "special" and "incidental" so they don't create gaps with indemnities.
- Clarify whether data breach / regulatory fines / IP claims would be carved out from any exclusion.

Attached: MSA_Stratos_Redlines_20261108.docx (redline)

Can your legal team take a quick pass and propose consolidated options? Procurement would like a short list of 2–3 fallback positions for internal approval. Happy to hop on a 20–30m call early this week.

Samantha — thanks and received. Karthik and I looped in legal (Laura). High level: Redwood's typical position is mutual exclusions for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, with explicit carve-outs for: (1) wilful misconduct, (2) IP indemnities, (3) payment obligations, and (4) narrow regulatory/consumer-protection fines tied to Customer's data processing.

To make procurement's life easier, Laura prepared three concise options (attached as a short annotated PDF). Quick summary below — pick whichever you prefer and we'll work that into the MSA redline:

Option A — Mutual exclusion (our preferred):
- Both parties waive consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages.
- Carve-outs for wilful misconduct, IP indemnity, and obligations to pay amounts due under an order form.
- Data breach/regulatory fines: treated as a separate limited carve-out only where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct caused the breach.

Option B — One-way exclusion in favor of Customer (procurement-friendly):
- Redwood agrees to a broader monetary exposure (i.e., limited liability cap for Redwood remains higher) but requests explicit carve-outs for IP indemnity and data-processing-related regulatory fines.
- Propose a tiered cap (Order Form cap higher for enterprise workloads).

Option C — Hybrid (compromise):
- Mutual exclusion for "consequential/special/incidental" but explicit carve-out for punitive and for statutory regulatory fines.
- If Stratos requires one-way, Redwood requests a higher liability cap and preservation of IP indemnity exceptions.

Action items for us: Laura to send sample clause language for each option and explain practical exposure (precedent and risk). Karthik: confirm whether the order form for this deal needs a separate, higher per-customer cap.

I'll attach Laura's notes now (MSA_Redwood_annotated_options.pdf). Can you confirm which option the Stratos procurement team prefers so we can iterate? If it's easier, we can schedule a call — I have availability Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the quick reply and for providing options. A few points from Stratos' legal perspective: we strongly prefer a one-way exclusion (i.e., Stratos' liability capped and exclusions apply only to Stratos) because of our downstream retail contracts. Procurement will not accept mutuality without significant commercial concessions.

If Redwood insists on mutual language, we would need:
- A materially lower Redwood liability cap (to keep risk allocation favorable for us).
- Confirmation that the carve-outs apply narrowly (IP indemnities, wilful misconduct) and do not expand to include ordinary negligence.

A couple of drafting notes (attached as a short mark-up):
1) Definitions: we propose replacing the long list of terms with a single defined term "Excluded Damages" and enumerating examples (including consequential/special/incidental/punitive). That helps procurement review faster.
2) Regulatory fines: Stratos will not accept a blanket carve-out in favor of Redwood. Any carve-out for regulatory fines must be limited to Redwood's willful misconduct or criminal acts.

Separately, please confirm whether Redwood expects any carve-outs for third-party cloud provider outages (we currently assume Redwood bears that risk when it results from Redwood's infrastructure choices).

I'll send over the redline (Stratos_counter_markup_20261109.docx) shortly.

Regards,
Anil Kapoor
Counsel, Stratos Retail

Anil / Samantha — thanks for the comments and the markup. I reviewed Stratos' proposed one-way approach. A few practical/legal points from Redwood's side:

1) Mutual exclusion is our standard because it avoids asymmetrical risk that can skew pricing and support models. If Stratos requires one-way language, Redwood would need commercial concessions (higher per-order-form caps, additional indemnities, or a pass-through of certain support costs).

2) On definitions: we prefer keeping separate defined terms ("Consequential Damages", "Incidental Damages", etc.) with short examples to avoid ambiguity. A single umbrella term can be acceptable only if examples are carefully drafted to preserve IP and payment exceptions.

3) Regulatory fines and data breach: Redwood can agree to a carve-out for regulatory fines and statutory penalties, but only where such fines are caused by Redwood's breach of its data-processing obligations or willful misconduct. We cannot accept unlimited exposure for third-party regulations triggered by Customer's use or misconfiguration.

4) Third-party cloud outages: Redwood will accept liability where the outage results from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct. We cannot accept liability for third-party provider downtime per se.

Proposed sample text (high level — we can produce mark-up):
- "Excluded Damages" means consequential, special, incidental or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, and loss of use.
- Each party's aggregate liability shall be limited to the amounts set forth in the applicable Order Form, except for liability arising from: (a) a party's wilful misconduct or gross negligence; (b) indemnification obligations for IP infringement; (c) a party's breach of confidentiality obligations; and (d) statutory regulatory fines to the extent caused by the responsible party's breach.

Happy to produce redlines for Option A and Option C that incorporate your drafting preferences. Given procurement timing, I'd propose a 30-minute call today to see whether a hybrid compromise (Option C) unlocks the deal. Laura

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Samantha / team — quick commercial note from our side: procurement timeline is tight and the account team would like to avoid a prolonged one-way vs mutual battle. Practically, Stratos has the leverage here (procurement) — our compromise recommendation:

- Accept Option C (Hybrid): mutual exclusion for consequential/special/incidental but carve out for punitive, IP indemnity, wilful misconduct and regulatory fines caused by the responsible party.
- Redwood agrees to increase the per-Order-Form cap for this enterprise Order Form by 2x compared to our standard starter cap, in exchange for mutual exclusions.
- If Stratos insists on a strict one-way exclusion, Redwood would need: (a) a commensurate increase in platform fees, or (b) an explicit carve-out preserving IP indemnities and regulatory carve-outs.

If helpful, we can do a 30-min call right now — otherwise let's lock in Option C and Laura will circulate a single consolidated redline for quick approval.

Thanks,
